source_reviews.independent_solution: Evaporation is molecules passing from the surface of a liquid into its gas/vapor phase. Liquid initial state, surface location and liquid-to-gas direction matter. It need not wait for boiling and is distinct from vapor-to-liquid condensation or solid-to-gas sublimation.

coverage.evidence: q02 supplies a liquid-water surface departure into vapor and asks the learner to name that process alongside the reverse phase path. source_reviews.independent_solution: Below boiling, molecular motion continues and speeds/energies are distributed. Some surface molecules have enough energy to overcome neighboring attractions and escape to gas, so evaporation can occur without whole-liquid boiling while the material remains liquid. Mere repetition that evaporation happens below boiling would not provide this explanation.

Distinguish gross outward evaporation from departure-minus-return net reduction.
